params.body:
## What

Inzichten gets a fourth tab, **Kaart** (`/insights?tab=kaart`): where the garages and traders on the platform are, per province, next to the car market there. It is the standalone map page of 29 September turned into a screen that reads the live database.

- **Figures on top:** garages in Belgium (and how many are active), traders in Belgium, our share of the car trade, accounts abroad.
- **Map:** the ten provinces and Brussels as a hand-built SVG, one dot per account (garage blue and sized by stock, trader amber, no module grey and off by default). Provinces are coloured by the number of garages or by our share of the car trade. Hovering or tapping a dot or a province shows the details, and the province and its table row light up together. No map library, no tiles, no external request.
- **Table per province:** garages, active, traders, stock, car trade (NACE 45.113), share, used-car registrations 2025, with a Belgium total. **The source line is printed under the table in the HTML itself**, with a link and a date per measure, so the numbers keep their source even if the script does not load.
- **Abroad:** one chip per country with its traders, garages and accounts without a module.

## Definitions (same as the source page)

- Garage = `module_1`; trader = `module_2` without `module_1`; the rest has no module. Demo accounts do not count (R P2-10.10).
- Active = a garage that added, changed, sold or deleted a vehicle in the **last 90 days** (`InsightsRepository::MAP_ACTIVE_DAYS`). The screen names the window.
- Stock = own vehicles for sale: on stock, not sold, not deleted, not in the bidding channel.
- Province = from the **postcode** (bpost ranges, Brussels as its own row, `App\Support\BelgianProvince`), so the table does not depend on coordinates. A Belgian account without a valid Belgian postcode only counts in the total, and the screen says how many.
- Dots use `dealers.latitude/longitude`, projected with the numbers stored next to the outlines. Null and 0,0 are counted in the table but not drawn, and the screen says how many.

## Why its own tab and not a section in "Klanten en omzet"

That tab answers *how much and when*. This one answers *where*, and it has its own request and its own script with about 11 kB of outline data. Its own tab means only people who open the map download that data and run that query, the 13 queries of the first tab do not grow, and the map can be shared as `?tab=kaart`.

## How it is built

- `resources/data/market-be.json`: the market reference figures, versioned, with `source`, `url`, `as_of` and a definition per measure (Statbel NACE 45.113 end of 2024 per head office; FOD Mobiliteit used-car registrations 2025 by holder address). The unused column of the source page is left out. `App\Support\MarketReference` reads it.
- `resources/data/be-provinces.json`: the outlines as SVG path data plus the projection (equirectangular, `x = (lng - 2.5) * 158.68`, `y = (51.55 - lat) * 250`, fitted to the source page's dots with a largest error of 0.05 units). Vite puts it inside the chunk, so it is a static build asset and not a blade string.
- `resources/js/insights-map.js`: a separate Vite entry, loaded only on this tab. It uses the same hand-built SVG approach as `insights.js`, adds nothing to `window`, and uses the `--brand-*` tokens, the existing `ins-` classes and Tailwind classes (arbitrary values where the theme's `!important` utilities would collide). No new `ui-` class, and refresh.css is not touched.
- `GET insights/map` (`insights.index.map`), guarded like the rest (administrator only). It is cached for an hour like the other insights (`map` added to the cache keys, so **Cijfers herberekenen** clears it). The refresh button now returns to the tab it was pressed on.
- UI text is in `resources/lang/{nl,fr,en,de}/insights.php` under `map`, with province names per language. Country names come from `Locale::getDisplayRegion` in the screen's language.

## Fix: a failed geocode stored 0,0

`Custom::getLongitudeAndLatitude` returned 0,0 when Google found nothing, and `DealerController::store` and `DealerLocationController::storeLocation` only checked for null, so the account was stored on the equator. `dealers.latitude/longitude` were `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so null could not even be stored.

- The helper returns null for both when there is no result, an error status, a timeout or connection error, or a reply of exactly 0,0. It now goes through Laravel's HTTP client instead of a bare `file_get_contents`, which also means the staging seal sees it. A new read-only `googlemaps` entry in `Outbound::services()` opens it on staging, and CLAUDE.md lists it.
- Both forms store what they get (null included).
- Migration `2026_09_30_130000_an_address_not_found_has_no_coordinates`: `dealers.latitude/longitude` become `FLOAT NULL DEFAULT NULL`, and `dealer_locations` gets default null. The ALTER is raw because `->change()` would turn FLOAT into DOUBLE. **Existing 0,0 rows are not rewritten.** A migration cannot tell a failed lookup from a row that never had an address. I could not count them on production from here, because production reads are blocked for this work. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dealers WHERE latitude = 0 AND longitude = 0` (and the same on `dealer_locations`) gives the number. The map tab reports them as "without coordinates".
- Side effect: `dealerResource` (partner API) now returns `null` instead of `0` for a dealer whose address was not found.

## Business rules

- New **R P2-10.26** (the map tab: definitions, sources, what is left out and said).
- **R P2-1.2** and **R P2-6.2** now say that an address not found gets empty coordinates, never 0,0.
- New finding `bevinding: mislukte-geocodering-bewaart-nul-nul`, resolved here.

## Tests

- `TheMapTabShowsWhereTheNetworkIsTest`: counts per province as differences against the answer before the test's own dealers (garage/trader/none, active window, stock excludes sold/deleted/bidding, demo excluded, Belgian account without a postcode counts in the total only, abroad per country). It also checks: 0,0 and null are counted but not drawn; every market figure carries source, https link and date; the data file and the outlines cover the same 11 rows; the postcode ranges; 403 for a non-administrator and a login redirect for a guest; the tab prints its source links and carries every id the script looks up; refresh returns to the tab.
- `AnAddressNotFoundHasNoCoordinatesTest`: ZERO_RESULTS, REQUEST_DENIED, 0,0 and a connection error give null, and a found address keeps its coordinates. A new dealer and a new location whose address is not found are stored with null, and a found location keeps its coordinates.
- Locally: `npm ci && npm run build`, then the full phpunit suite (BuildContractTest included), PHPStan with no errors, and pint on the new PHP files.
params.title: Inzichten: a map tab with the dealers per province against the market
